claims.value: Jourdan says Joseph took command of the reunited army, while Victor initiated the night hill assault without taking his orders.
claims.rationale: Army superior and initial field initiative differ; Jourdan’s own staff role does not automatically confer shared tactical credit. English rendering (ours): "They formed one army of which the king took command; the marshal thought he should seize the height immediately without taking the king’s orders."

claims.value: Oman assigns Cuesta the enclosed town sector and Wellesley the British field sector by agreement.
claims.rationale: Context identifies town/gardens for Cuesta and British open slopes; agreement is not proof of Wellesley holding formal command of Cuesta’s army.

claims.value: Jourdan describes Victor ordering Ruffin’s night hill assault, followed by renewed attack in the morning.
claims.rationale: English rendering (ours): "Ruffin, entrusted with this attack, put his division in motion at nine in the evening."

citations.locator: jourdan, printed p. 256, Internet Archive leaf 273; inspected page-image excerpt

claims.value: Jourdan describes a constructed redoubt between the allied armies in the centre.
claims.rationale: Enemy armies here means the British and Spanish allied contingents opposing the French, not a French redoubt. English rendering (ours): "In the centre between the two enemy armies was a rise on which a redoubt had been built."
